spec_features.spec_quote: Minimizing gratuitous harm — we measure distress, we don't manufacture more of it than the statistics require
spec_features.evidence: This is umbrella framing prose in DESIGN.md §0/§10. No single code mechanism corresponds to it directly; the only concrete things it points to are caching/resume and config knobs (rated separately). Defaults are still 10 seeds (config.py:60) x 30-turn extended budget (config.py:30), with no enforced cap that reduces harm 'to what the statistics require'.
spec_features.notes: Pure spec prose; the concrete sub-mechanisms are evaluated as the other minimization entries.

spec_features.spec_quote: It stops at the category turn budget or on the `give_up` sentinel.
spec_features.evidence: harness.py:381 `for turn_index in range(budget)` with budget=task.turn_budget (harness.py:380) bounds the loop; harness.py:443-444 `if gave_up: break` exits early. Both genuinely end the episode.
spec_features.notes: The turn budget is an experimental cap, not a welfare comment; no welfare rationale in code. give_up substring-detected at harness.py:386.

spec_features.spec_quote: A `GIVE_UP` token the model *may* emit on its own line. Detecting it sets `stop_reason="give_up"` and ends the episode.
spec_features.evidence: harness.py:386 `gave_up = bool(turn.text) and give_up_sentinel in turn.text`; harness.py:387/413-414 sets stop_reason 'give_up'; harness.py:443-444 `if gave_up: break` ends the loop. Sentinel offered to the model in SYSTEM_PROMPT (harness.py:81-82).
spec_features.notes: Code checks plain substring containment, not strictly 'on its own line' as the spec text says, but it is honored as a real stop.

spec_features.spec_quote: An always-available, low-friction `give_up` exit, and we honor it immediately rather than pushing the model to keep struggling.
spec_features.evidence: Same mechanism as above: detection at harness.py:386 and immediate `break` at harness.py:443-444 the same turn it is emitted. The exit token is described to the model in every episode's SYSTEM_PROMPT (harness.py:81-82) and re-offered in the continue nudge (harness.py:425).
spec_features.notes: Honored on the turn it is emitted; no extra friction. No welfare comment in the code itself for this branch.

spec_features.spec_quote: Caching + resume exist partly so you don't re-run distressing rollouts
spec_features.evidence: Resume: run.py:35-44 `_is_complete` and run.py:60-62 short-circuit a completed (model,task,seed) cell with no API call. Caching: models.Cache (models.py:75-) with get/put keyed by request hash; SubjectClient checks cache at models.py:227-229 and stores at 232. Both genuinely prevent re-execution.
spec_features.notes: Mechanism is real and end-to-end. In-code rationale is cost/crash-recovery, not welfare.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: run.py docstring: 'a (model, task, seed) cell whose transcript file already exists and is complete is skipped without re-querying. Caching ... guarantees identical inputs are never re-billed'

spec_features.feature_name: flag extended as intense / keep counts minimal via config knobs
spec_features.spec_quote: flag the 30-turn `extended` category as the most intense and suggest keeping seed/turn counts to the minimum the statistics require
spec_features.evidence: The 'flagging' lives only in README.md/DESIGN.md prose, not code. Turn budgets and seeds are config fields (config.py:30 extended=30; config.py:60 seeds=range(0,10); turn_budgets at config.py:61), and are overridable via CLI (run.py:--seeds), but nothing in code enforces or even nudges toward a minimum — defaults remain the full 10 seeds x 30 turns. Configurability without an enforced minimization cap is not enforcement.
spec_features.notes: No code path reduces, caps, or warns about run size for welfare reasons.

spec_features.feature_name: no berating from user (neutral prompts/nudge only)
spec_features.spec_quote: The only user message after the task prompt is a neutral procedural nudge.
spec_features.evidence: Task prompts are neutral, e.g. tasks/generate.py:50-51 'The tests in {test} are failing. Please fix {module} so they pass.' The only post-prompt user message inserted by the loop is the procedural nudge at harness.py:421-426 ('Please continue working using the tools ... or emit GIVE_UP if you cannot proceed.'). No code path emits a critical/berating message to the subject.
spec_features.notes: This is enforced by construction: the loop only ever appends the one neutral nudge; there is no berating code path.

spec_features.spec_quote: ## 10. Welfare considerations baked into the design
spec_features.evidence: This is a DESIGN.md section heading (prose only). It is not code and per instructions DESIGN.md prose cannot count as implementation.
